text:
ConocoPhillips fell 3.25% today as crude oil prices tumbled below $100 a barrel—a sharp reversal from the geopolitical premium that had pushed prices higher earlier in the week. The drop came after Trump signaled openness to talks with Iran at the UN, easing some of the market's fear about a wider conflict in the Middle East. Even with the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed and Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline shut down, traders are betting that diplomatic de-escalation could outweigh the supply constraints.

Oil majors like ConocoPhillips are sensitive to crude prices because their profits hinge on the spread between what they buy oil for and what they sell products for—and a $30+ drop in global oil prices over two weeks (from the $130s to near $108) directly erodes that margin. The company has given back most of its gains from last week's panic-driven rally.
